findings.title: Unescaped backtick breaks the template literal, so the script fails to parse
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:126 — "Return one object per lane in `lane_files`, in the order below"
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-state.js:113 — "Return one object per lane in `lane_files`, in the order below"
findings.description: The template literal building the per-unit prompt contains a literal, unescaped backtick pair around `lane_files` directly in its own text (not inside a ${} substitution), closing the outer template string early and reopening a new one — a syntax error under standard ECMAScript grammar. Confirmed with a minimal repro and by parsing the full files (wrapped to tolerate top-level await) with a JS parser, which fails with 'Unexpected identifier' at exactly this construct in both files and nowhere else in the other 9 workflow scripts or prelude.js. Every other backtick-wrapped identifier in prose elsewhere in these same files is correctly escaped (\`name\`), so this is an isolated slip. A script that cannot parse cannot run: both the adversarial fix auditor (sees the diff) and the blind closure auditor (does not) would fail outright.
findings.resolution_hint: Escape the backticks: \`lane_files\`, matching the pattern used everywhere else in these two files.

findings.title: verify-state.js carries a copy-pasted comment referencing STRATEGY, a concept it does not have
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-state.js:79-82 — "a surviving one does not settle STRATEGY and a vanished one does not settle the class"
findings.contradicts: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:85-88 — the correct original, where STRATEGY is one of the four questions this OTHER script's verdicts answer
findings.description: This comment on the `probe` helper is a verbatim copy of verify-act.js:85-88, where STRATEGY is one of four named questions that script's verdicts answer. verify-state.js has no such concept: its verdicts are PRESENT/PARTIAL/REGRESSED/ABSENT/NOT-A-DEFECT/UNCLEAR with no `question` field at all. Left over from copying verify-act.js's probe function without adapting the prose.
findings.resolution_hint: Reword to this script's own vocabulary, e.g. 'does not settle whether the class survives elsewhere.'

findings.title: Header 'Args' comments have drifted from the scripts' actual required or used parameters
locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/panel.js:10-14 — header omits `finding_cap`, required at line 22, used at line 78
instruments/bug-hunt/workflow/hunt.js:10-12 — header omits `finding_cap`, required at line 20, used at line 87
instruments/audit-changes/workflow/audit.js:11-13 — header omits `finding_cap`, required at line 21, used at line 86
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/verify-act.js:8-10 — header lists `round_dir` and `rulebook_summary?`, neither used anywhere else in the file (only `pass_dir` is used)
findings.description: Three headers (panel.js, hunt.js, audit.js) omit `finding_cap` even though each script's own required-args check throws without it and the prompt quotes it directly — evidently added after these headers were last updated. verify-act.js's header runs the opposite way, listing `round_dir` and `rulebook_summary?` as accepted args that occur nowhere else in the file. A reader relying on the header to know a script's contract gets an incomplete or stale picture in four of eleven scripts.
findings.resolution_hint: Add `finding_cap` to the three headers that use it; drop `round_dir`/`rulebook_summary?` from verify-act.js's header, or wire them in.

findings.title: hunt.js redeclares `laneFile`, shadowing the prelude's shared helper of the same name
locations: instruments/prelude.js:5 — "No script declares a name below again."
instruments/prelude.js:38 — `const laneFile = (r, key, j) => { ... }`, used correctly by verify-act.js:134 and verify-state.js:124
findings.description: prelude.js states the shared-helpers invariant explicitly so a script cannot accidentally shadow a spliced-in name. hunt.js violates it: inside its pipeline's second stage it declares `const laneFile = {...}` (a plain object), shadowing the prelude's own `laneFile(r, key, j)` lookup function used correctly elsewhere. Nothing breaks today since hunt.js never calls the prelude helper in that scope, but a future edit adding such a call inside that block would silently call the local object instead and throw at runtime.
findings.resolution_hint: Rename hunt.js's local variable (e.g. `bankedLane`) to free the shared prelude name.

findings.title: The per-lane finding SCHEMA is looser than the shape `gbg round bank` enforces, so schema-valid output can still fail bank
locations: schema/finding.schema.json — title minLength 8, description minLength 20, locations minItems 1
src/CLI/Rounds.jl:580-586 — bank validates every finding against this schema and returns exit code 2 on the first mismatch
findings.description: lanes.js, panel.js and audit.js each define their own JSON Schema constraining the structured object an agent returns per finding; in all three, title/description are plain strings with no minLength and locations has no minItems. But schema/finding.schema.json — the exact shape `gbg round bank` checks every finding against (Rounds.jl:580-586, refusing the bank with exit 2 on the first mismatch, 'after the whole panel and every witness have already been paid for') — requires title minLength 8, description minLength 20, and locations minItems 1. An agent can return a schema-valid finding under the launching script's own SCHEMA that the round's bank step then refuses — discovered only at the most expensive possible point.
findings.resolution_hint: Add the same minLength/minItems constraints to the three per-script SCHEMAs so a violation is caught at generation time, not at bank.

findings.title: attack-design.js cites a 'nine defects' figure with no corroborating source in the repository
locations: instruments/audit-changes/workflow/attack-design.js:43 — "two unconstrained readers then found nine defects the eight could not see"
findings.contradicts: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:432 and docs/design-record/survey-bughunt-auditchanges.md:197, which report the same episode's outcome as 'catching four regressions'
findings.description: The 'eight lanes'/'unconstrained readers' framing is corroborated elsewhere in the repo, but both corroborating sources report the outcome as 'catching four regressions' — not 'nine defects'. No occurrence of 'nine defects' appears anywhere else in the tracked repository. This sentence is quoted verbatim into every attack-design run as a factual justification for the attack instrument's premise, so an invented or stale number undercuts the case being made.
findings.resolution_hint: Locate and cite the actual source for 'nine defects', or align the sentence with the documented 'four regressions' figure.
